name: Bathing in the Unstruck Sound
previous_label: Prasarita Padottanasana — Wide-Legged Standing Forward Fold (asana framing, retired 2026-10)

dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: anāhate pātrakarṇe 'bhagnaśabde sariddrute | śabdabrahmaṇi niṣṇātaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
dharana.rendering: One who is steeped in sound-Brahman, the unstruck (anāhata) and unbroken sound that rushes like a river and is heard by the fit ear, reaches the supreme Brahman.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: niṣṇāta means both 'well-versed' and 'bathed in'; the sound is an inner sound heard by an ear made competent by yoga. Bäumer compares the sound to a waterfall, and Chaudhri adds 'the continuous sound of a river flowing, or by closing the ears' (both as printed in The Mystery Within). The verse itself names neither a waterfall nor closing the ears.

checked_against: Lakshmanjoo lineage: A blog transcribing Lakshmanjoo's teaching (sannyastheatre.gallery) and an Italian study page label verse 38 'Dhāraṇā 15'; not checked in a print Lakshmanjoo edition.
GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y12 (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)
numbering_variants.hatha_es: dharana 15 = a variant of verse 42 (piṇḍa-mantra fading into void); non-standard, not followed (the previous draft of this door followed it)

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 38 does not prescribe a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: a continuous inner stream of sound
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a continuous stream of sound flowing through the vessel of the ear, followed inward until the listener is immersed in it.
geometry.svg_hint: a soft wavy stream flowing into an ear outline and widening into open space
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Gross to subtle sound
reaction.summary: School metaphor: attention moves from outer noise to a steady inner stream and is immersed in it. Not a medical or chemical claim.

breath.lands_in: quiet breath that does not compete with listening
breath.cue: Natural, quiet breath, about four in and six out if counting helps. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Orient toward sound: first steady outer sound, then the subtle inner hum
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: A steady, unbroken stream of sound, followed from outer to inner
attention.secondary: Being immersed in it rather than analysing it

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: One who is steeped in sound-Brahman, the unstruck (anāhata) and unbroken sound that rushes like a river and is heard by the fit ear, reaches the supreme Brahman.
adiyogi.method_summary: Begin with a steady natural sound if helpful (running water, wind, a fan), then let attention move to the subtle continuous hum heard when the room is quiet. Stay immersed in that unbroken sound like bathing in a river. If covering the ears, rest the palms lightly over them without pressing.

honesty.disclosure: Door 015 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 15 (verse 38) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 015 is dharana 15, verse 38. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
Reframed from the earlier posture framing on 2026-10-06; awaiting guardian re-review. The previous review covered the posture framing only.
Numbering correction: the previous draft of this door followed hatha.es's non-standard numbering (dharana 15 = a variant of verse 42 (piṇḍa-mantra fading into void)). Rebuilt to Singh's verse 38.

legacy.disclosure: This [retired posture]↔method link is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device, not ancient canon. [retired posture] and dharana 015 are paired by school index, not by classical one-to-one lineage.
legacy.notes: Edition note: school index = dharana 015 as labeled at hatha.es (piṇḍamantra → ardhendu-bindu-nādānta-śūnya). Many printed editions place related Sanskrit near verse ~42 (e.g. Jaideva Singh / commentary lines); numbering of ‘dharana 15’ vs ‘verse N’ varies by edition. Soft experiential rhyme (gross form thinning toward quiet) is noted but not elevated to inner_logic without stronger textual warrant.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If listening inward makes a ringing or other sound in the ears feel distressing, stop and listen to ordinary sounds in the room instead. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.open_seat_alternate: Keep hands on blocks or a chair with a concave spine; skip crown-to-floor. Soften knees if hamstrings or low back protest.
legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Use support under hands or head; avoid dumping weight onto the neck. If dizziness appears in the [retired posture], come up slowly with hands on hips.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 015: bathing in the unstruck sound. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 15, verse 38.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Any easy seat, or lie down. The map is a stream of sound flowing through the ear.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Body still. Eyes closed. Orient toward sound.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Quiet natural breath, four in, six out if you like. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Listen to a steady outer sound, then to the subtle hum underneath. Let it flow like a river. Bathe in it.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: outer noise gives way to an inner stream. Metaphor only.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 38: one steeped in the unstruck, unbroken sound that rushes like a river reaches the supreme. Just listen.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Let ordinary sounds come back. Open the eyes slowly.
